terms.gloss: oh, all right; very well then (giving in)
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 573: Quid istīc? quandō ita vīs: dī bene vortant.
Plaut. Rud. 1331b: Quid istīc? necessum est, videō
terms.comment: Literally “what there?”, as if “what is one to say to that?” In each of these places the speaker stops arguing and gives way.

phrases.latin: Quid istīc? quandō ita vīs: dī bene vortant. Spondeō.
phrases.english: Oh, very well; since you will have it so, heaven bless it. I give my consent.

phrases.latin: Nihil opust rescīscat. — Quid istīc? nōn rescīscet, nē timē.
phrases.english: There’s no need for her to find out. — All right, all right; she won’t find out, don’t worry.

sources: Lewis & Short: istic
